If an integer is divisible by 10, then it is even.

originalQuestion.prompt:
Translate this [argument](ref:argument) into propositional notation and decide whether it is [valid](ref:validity). Explain your reasoning.

If the application is accepted, an interview is scheduled. If an interview is scheduled, a confirmation is sent. The application is accepted. Therefore a confirmation is sent.
originalQuestion.officialAnswer: Let $p$ mean the application is accepted, $q$ mean an interview is scheduled, and $r$ mean a confirmation is sent. The [premises](ref:argument) are $p\to q$, $q\to r$, and $p$; the [conclusion](ref:argument?repeat) is $r$. [Modus ponens](ref:modus-ponens) first gives $q$ and then $r$, so the [argument](ref:argument?repeat) is [valid](ref:validity).

originalQuestion.prompt: In the three-peg [Tower of Hanoi](ref:hanoi) puzzle, move a stack of $n$ differently sized disks to another peg. Move one exposed disk at a time and never place a larger disk on a smaller one. Let $H(n)$ be the minimum number of moves. State $H(0)$ and derive a recurrence for $H(n)$.
originalQuestion.officialAnswer: $H(0)=0$ and $H(n)=2H(n-1)+1$ for $n\geq1$. The usual construction moves the smaller stack to the spare peg, moves the largest disk to its destination, and moves the smaller stack onto it, using this many moves. For a lower bound, before the largest disk's first move the entire smaller stack must have moved to one other peg, requiring at least $H(n-1)$ moves. After its last move to the destination, the smaller stack is entirely on a different peg and needs at least $H(n-1)$ further moves. Those two stages and at least one largest-disk move give the same lower bound, so the construction is [optimal](ref:optimality).

originalQuestion.instructions: Construct a small countermodel and justify it.
originalQuestion.prompt: There are exactly two visitors, Ada and Ben, and exactly two guides, Gia and Hal. Specify who guides whom so each visitor has a guide but no guide serves every visitor. Explain how this separates the two quantifier orders.
originalQuestion.answer: For example, Gia guides only Ada and Hal guides only Ben. Every visitor has a guide, so $\forall v\exists g\,G(g,v)$ holds. Gia does not guide Ben and Hal does not guide Ada, so $\exists g\forall v\,G(g,v)$ fails. The witness may vary with the visitor.
